description: §5.2 rule 2, S457 bullet event-handler text from data: `ONCLICK=${@code}` is not a spelling the compiler wires as a listener, so it would be WRITTEN as handler text built from data — refused.
rationale: §5.2 rule 2 (S457): "Where an emitter would instead WRITE an `on…` attribute (rule 1's name test) from data — a spelling it does not wire as a listener, such as `ONCLICK=${…}` … — the write SHALL be a compile error (E-ATTR-INTERP-EXECUTABLE)". Before S457 it compiled to `el.setAttribute("ONCLICK", String(value))`, which the browser compiles as an onclick handler.
